matches.text:
or mass. Naive objects are easy to understand and to work with, at the cost of ignoring some aspects of reality.
For applications requiring aware objects, datetime and time objects have an optional time zone information attribute, tzinfo , that can be set to an instance of a subclass of the abstract tzinfo class. These tzinfo objects capture information about the offset from UTC time, the time zone name, and whether daylight saving time is in effect.
Only one concrete tzinfo class, the timezone class, is supplied by the datetime module. The timezone class can represent simple time zones with fixed offsets from UTC, such as UTC itself or North American EST and EDT time zones. Supporting time zones at deeper levels of detail is up to the application. The rules for time adjustment across the world are more political than rational, change frequently, and there is no standard suitable for every application aside from UTC.

arguments.answer:
Create an aware datetime by supplying a tzinfo object (e.g. an instance of ``datetime.timezone`` or any ``tzinfo`` subclass) when constructing the datetime, or by converting a naive datetime with ``datetime.replace(tzinfo=…)``. Then use ``datetime.astimezone()`` to convert it to another zone.

Example:
```python
import datetime as dt

# Build an aware datetime in UTC
aware_utc = dt.datetime(2024, 5, 1, 12, 0, tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc)
# or: aware_utc = dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc)

# Convert to another timezone, e.g. US/Eastern (using the zoneinfo database)
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
eastern = ZoneInfo('US/Eastern')
aware_eastern = aware_utc.astimezone(eastern)
print(aware_eastern)  # 2024-05-01 08:00:00-04:00
```
The ``astimezone`` call returns a new ``datetime`` whose ``tzinfo`` is set to the target zone and whose date‑time values are adjusted so the instant in UTC is unchanged.

Key points from the documentation:
* An aware ``datetime`` must have its ``tzinfo`` attribute set to an instance of a ``tzinfo`` subclass (e.g., ``datetime.timezone`` or a custom subclass)【0†source】.
* ``datetime.now(timezone.utc)`` is the recommended way to obtain the current UTC aware datetime【0†source】.
* ``datetime.astimezone(tz)`` converts an aware datetime to another timezone, adjusting the clock values while preserving the same UTC moment【4†source】.
